title: A 2-Ton Shark Launches 10 Feet Out of the Water to Catch One Seal

scenes.text: A two-ton shark launches ten feet out of the water.
scenes.keywords: great white shark breaching jumping water

scenes.text: Seal Island, South Africa. Great whites attack seals from straight below.
The run starts 65 feet down, in the dark, and hits the surface at over 20 miles an hour.
The seal gets a tenth of a second to react.
scenes.keywords: cape fur seal swimming ocean surface

scenes.text: The hit carries the whole shark clear of the sea. Over 4,000 pounds. In the air.
scenes.keywords: great white shark breach slow motion

scenes.text: And it works about half the time. The other half, ten feet of air for nothing.

description:
Great white sharks at Seal Island in False Bay, South Africa, hunt by rocketing up from below and can breach up to 3 metres (10 feet) clear of the water.
They begin the attack from as deep as 20 metres and reach more than 20 miles an hour on the way up; an adult great white can be 6 metres long and weigh over 2,000 kilograms. Even so, only about half the attacks succeed, and fewer in bright light.
Would you rather be the seal or the shark? Comment below.
first_comment: Scientists tagged the sharks and found the whole climb from 65 feet down takes just 7 to 16 seconds. Which animal would you least want sneaking up from below?
